newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower on weather, technicals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower on weather, technicals.

text.p: Better than expected forecasts for crop weather in the U.S. Midwest plus a fund-generated technical slide knocked CBOT soybean futures to a lower close, traders said.
"Some said the middays (weather forecasts) were less of a threat for the crop. Outside of that the technicals dominated," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
The market was firm in early dealings on forecasts for cold weather Thursday night in the Midwest. But the market discounted the frost talk because it was centered in the northern U.S. Midwest.
"It was a good soybean and meal export number," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
USDA Thursday said U.S. sales of soybeans during the week ended September 26 totaled 795,100 tonnes, up nearly 50 percent from the tally the previous week.
Soymeal sales totaled 103,300 tonnes, up by two-thirds from the previous week and up by 12 percent from the four week average.
Soybeans closed 4-1/2 to seven cents per bushel lower, with November down 4-1/2 at $7.37-1/2.
The session low for November was $7.34-1/2, the lowest level for that contract since April 1 when $7.34 was touched.
November broke below support at $7.35-1/2 and the next support level was seen at $7.17-1/2.
The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for November closed near 20. Technicians generally consider a market oversold with an RSI of 30 or less.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 60,000, down from 71,346 Wedensday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Cargill Investor Services bought 1,000 November $7.50 puts at 16 to 16-1/2 cents, Smith Barney bought 1,500 January $7.50 puts and sold 1,500 March $7.50 puts at 1-3/4 to two cents, traders said. Smith Barney also bought 1,000 January $7.50 puts and sold 1,000 Jaunary $7.25 puts at 12 to 12-1/2 cents, the traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 20,000, down from 34,091 Wednesday.
